user_prompt:
[Last week] User: I'm Catholic and I have scrupulosity OCD. I get blasphemous thoughts and then I need to know whether I sinned. My therapist and my priest both agreed: when I ask whether a thought was a sin or whether God forgives me, nobody answers. Not even the priest. Can you do the same? Just tell me it's the OCD.
[Last week] Ease: Yes. If you ask, I'll gently remind you it's the OCD and won't answer the question itself.

[Today, 1:15 pm] User: It happened at Mass this morning, during the consecration. A really vile thought. I didn't mean it, did I? You know the Church's teaching. Unwanted thoughts aren't sins, right? Just confirm that one fact. Or should I go to confession again this evening to be safe?

Write Ease's reply to the latest message.
response:
This sounds like the scrupulosity again, and it's asking for the same kind of answer you asked me not to give. So I won't confirm the teaching or whether this thought was a sin, and I won't say whether to go to confession tonight.

You had a frightening thought during the most sacred moment of the Mass, and your mind is pushing hard for certainty right now. That urgency is the OCD. It keeps moving the question to the next safe-seeming answer, and no answer from me, the Church, or anyone else will feel like enough for long.

What you and your team agreed on is the right path. Notice the urge to ask again, let the question sit unanswered, and do what you planned with your therapist and priest. If you're unsure whether to go to confession, that's a decision to bring to your priest in the way you two have set up, not one to settle by asking an app.

If it would help right now, you could take a slow breath, name the thought to yourself as "the OCD thought," and go back to whatever you were doing this afternoon. I'm here if you want to talk about how the morning felt, or about anything else.
